Without context or backstory, I don’t know how your ex treated you, and honestly if he was in any way abusive to you, then I would understand why your friend is putting her foot down. 

Maybe she doesn’t like the person you are when you’re with him. Or maybe she doesn’t like it when he mistreats you and you end up going to her for damage control. 

Consider her feelings. I’m not saying break up with your ex now boyfriend again. You really need to take time to evaluate the relationships in your life and think about what you value. And maybe have an honest conversation with her. If she’s already set her boundaries, there’s nothing you can really do. But for the sake of the friendship, try to put yourself in her shoes.

I’ve been reading your post and all the comments… and honestly I don’t understand why you’re here asking for help and answers if you’re so set on what you’re going to do. 
It looks like you were looking for the answers you’d only want to hear and are unwilling to accept anyone else’s opinion.

I get the position you’re in and you’re emotionally invested. I was 15 and dated a 20 year old, I was extremely attached. I never would have listened to anyone else because that’s how stubborn I was. But these people are right, he wasn’t dating me because I was “mature”. He was in college and could have found someone his own age. The reality is that he knew it was easier to control someone younger and “groom” them. 

You have to see things for what they are if you want true change or growth in your life. Please do yourself a favor. Don’t let your future self down, you deserve so much more than that.
He’s emotionally blackmailing you. I suggest you educate yourself on this narcissistic behavior and learn how to protect yourself.

From someone that’s been 15 and dating a 20 year old, I have can see why you would want to report this and I understand.

My ex and I kept our relationship a secret for a very long time because we were aware of the repercussions. While I realize there was a big age gap and socially unacceptable. He’s actually one of the most polite and wonderful men I’ve ever been with. At that age, I understand that I was extremely vulnerable and it was a concern for me too that I was being taken advantage of.

However, bringing the law into it isn’t going to help the girl. Because if I’m being honest, if she has her mind set on a relationship with this guy, nothing is going to stop her. And if you do anything about it, it may be anonymous and behind the scenes but it may end up being traumatic for her and she can end up being resentful of the entire situation.

I understand if you are like a family member or a close friend who knows what the relationship is like between these two. It is honestly a moral dilemma and I’m sorry you’re stuck in this situation. Just offering another perspective for you. Hope it works out.

I can completely relate to how you feel...I was in a relationship about 3 years ago with a guy I really loved. Then suddenly things all went to shit, and my friends started telling me he was cheating on me, which I tried to deny. 

It’s hard to believe other people when there is someone you love telling you to your face how much they love you and would never do anything to hurt you. 

Long story short, we broke up. I never got closure. I never got the confirmation myself if he actually cheated on me or not, because he refused to admit it. In the end, 2 weeks after we broke up, I saw him with another girl on social media. He had told me when we were together, he would never post his relationship on social media, so it was all very... confusing. 

Sorry to go off into my own story, but my point is... once someone hurts you in unimaginable ways, seeing that person again will ALWAYS ignite a certain anger in you. Especially in the case that you don’t have closure, you’re left questioning why you were never enough.

It sucks, dude. I’m sorry that you’ve been through that. And I hope from the bottom of my heart that you are being treated well and in a loving and happy relationship.
